Conflict: Material and Design, Manufacture, and Circularity agents recommend recycled monomaterial Polypropylene to maximize recyclability and lower carbon footprint, whereas the In-Service agent rejects this in favor of virgin ABS/PC to ensure impact durability and prevent suction leaks.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent; Circularity Agent; In-Service Agent
Decision: Monomaterial Post-Consumer Recycled (PCR) Polypropylene (PP) with structural ribs.
Rationale: Applying the priority hierarchy, engineering feasibility is maintained by utilizing structural ribbing to compensate for PCR PP's lower impact strength compared to ABS. This choice aligns with sustainability best practices by maximizing recycled content and ensuring end-of-life recyclability as a monomaterial, avoiding high-impact virgin plastics.
ESPR Citation: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (d) & (h): design for recycling and use of recycled materials

Conflict: The Manufacture agent recommends direct snap-fit joints to eliminate fasteners and simplify assembly, while the Material and Design, In-Service, and Circularity agents reject this because snap-fits are highly prone to breaking during repair and EOL disassembly, advocating for reversible mechanical fasteners.
Agents Involved: Manufacture Agent; Material and Design Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Reversible mechanical fasteners (standardized screws with threaded metal inserts).
Rationale: Under the priority hierarchy, engineering feasibility for repeated repair and non-destructive EOL disassembly is prioritized over initial manufacturing speed. Snap-fits are highly susceptible to fatigue and shearing, which would limit the product's service life and prevent high-quality recycling.
ESPR Citation: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (c) & (d): ease of disassembly, repair, and recycling

Conflict: Material and Design and Manufacture agents recommend a rare-earth-free synchronous reluctance motor to avoid critical raw materials and manufacturing emissions, whereas In-Service and Circularity agents recommend a high-efficiency BLDC motor to ensure high suction efficiency and durability during the use phase.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: High-efficiency modular Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with easily extractable neodymium magnets.
Rationale: A vacuum cleaner's primary function relies heavily on suction power density and energy efficiency. A synchronous reluctance motor would be too heavy and bulky, reducing suction performance. Selecting a modular BLDC motor designed for easy disassembly preserves use-phase efficiency (sustainability in use) and enables the circular recovery of neodymium magnets at EOL.
ESPR Citation: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (g) & (d): energy efficiency and ease of recycling

Conflict: Manufacture and Circularity agents recommend using the main aerodynamic suction airflow for cooling to eliminate extra components and potting, whereas In-Service and Material and Design agents recommend an active cooling fan with dedicated heatsinks and filters to prevent motor overheating when the main suction path is clogged.
Agents Involved: Manufacture Agent; Circularity Agent; In-Service Agent; Material and Design Agent
Decision: Forced-air cooling using main suction airflow with open, conformal-coated PCBs and washable filters.
Rationale: This option balances engineering feasibility and sustainability. Utilizing the existing suction airflow eliminates the raw material footprint of auxiliary fans and heavy heatsinks, while washable filters and thermal cutoff sensors protect the motor from overheating without needing complex, unrecyclable potting compounds.
ESPR Citation: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (e): avoidance of solutions detrimental to recycling

Conflict: The Manufacture agent recommends a monolithic integrated design to minimize production complexity and assembly waste, while Material and Design, In-Service, and Circularity agents demand a fully modular, plug-and-play architecture to enable easy repair, component swapping, and EOL recycling.
Agents Involved: Manufacture Agent; Material and Design Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Fully modular architecture with plug-and-play functional modules.
Rationale: Although monolithic designs reduce initial manufacturing complexity, they fail sustainability best practices because a single component failure forces the disposal of the entire appliance. Modularity drastically extends the product life and facilitates circularity, outweighing the initial manufacturing complexity.
ESPR Citation: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (c): ease of repair and remanufacturing

Conflict: The Material and Design agent recommends a corded AC power system with an automatic cord reel to improve storage convenience, whereas In-Service and Manufacture agents reject this mechanism due to its high failure rate and manufacturing complexity, preferring a simple, user-replaceable heavy-duty power cord.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; In-Service Agent; Manufacture Agent
Decision: Corded AC power with a user-replaceable heavy-duty power cord (manual wrap).
Rationale: A simple, user-replaceable heavy-duty cord satisfies engineering feasibility by eliminating the complex automatic reel mechanism, which is a common failure point. This choice ensures the longest possible product service life and simplifies both manufacturing and repair.
ESPR Citation: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (a) & (r): durability and waste prevention
